**Finding: Deviation (high severity) — Section 6.1 Exclusivity**

**What I found.** Section 6.1 imposes a genuine exclusive-dealing obligation on our client: the Company may not participate in any similar internet project for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products, and HDI takes the exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand online.

**Why it fails the fallback:**
- **Duration** — the restriction runs "during the term of this Agreement," and Section 4.1 auto-renews the term for successive one-year periods indefinitely. Exiting requires 90 days' notice *and* triggers a Termination Payment under Section 4.2, so there is no clean 12-month boundary.
- **No performance exit** — the agreement has no service-level regime and no termination-for-breach clause. The only performance-linked exit (Section 1.6, failure to launch within 70 days) is a one-off right that lapses once the Site goes live.

That combination — exclusivity for the full term with no ongoing performance-based release — is the rule's walk-away scenario.

**Direction check.** Section 6.3 (HDI's two-year non-compete) and Section 5.2 (our exclusive editorial control) run in our favour and are left untouched. Only the covenant binding the Company is redlined.

**Redline (fallback, validated ok:true).** Because HDI's reciprocal covenant in 6.3 forms part of the bargain, outright deletion would be disproportionate. Two minimal edits to p0037:
1. "during the term of this Agreement" → "during the period of twelve (12) months following the Effective Date"
2. Added an automatic release: the restriction terminates "without further notice, penalty or liability, upon any failure by HDI to meet any delivery date or service or performance level required under this Agreement."

Noted but not separately flagged: the open-ended "companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled" sweep — the core scope is anchored to the defined term "Deerskin Products," which satisfies the fallback's product-category requirement.
